# UniSuperMimic: Learning Humanoid Robot Motion Tracking Using a Differentiable World Model

This chapter introduces [Motphys' Uni-SuperMimic](https://github.com/Motphys/Uni-SuperMimic): it is a independent reproduction of [SuperMimic](https://supermimic.github.io/) conducted at UniLab, aiming to enable Unitree G1 to track various reference motions. The project provides LAFAN1 and BONES-SEED data processing, training, evaluation, and video export, supporting mjwarp, MuJoCo, and Motrix backends.

![UniSuperMimic Policy and Reference Action Comparison ](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Motphys/Uni-SuperMimic/main/docs/assets/supermimic_comparison.gif)

*Figure 1: Upstream simulation demonstration. The physical robot represents the policy output, and the blue silhouette indicates the reference action. Source: [Uni-SuperMimic](https://github.com/Motphys/Uni-SuperMimic).*

## Method: Simulation, World Model, and Policy

SuperMimic first collects state and motion conversion data through physical simulation, and trains a differentiable dynamics model; the policy then updates it via short-term imagined trajectory and time backpropagation in the world model. The simulator provides the training data, eliminating the need for derivative calculations on the physical simulation engine itself. The world model and the motion tracking policy are updated together during training.

```text
参考动作 + 机器人状态 → 策略动作 → 物理仿真 → 转移数据
                                    ↓
                           学习可微世界模型
                                    ↓
                       想象轨迹 → 梯度更新策略
```

The research results of the paper, the independent implementation of Motphys, and this chapter's tutorial should be understood separately. The screenshots show community demonstrations; the repository labels its implementation as reproduction, and it cannot be directly regarded as the original code of the paper author. No training or evaluation has been conducted in this chapter yet.

## Start from the LAFAN1 route

The environments listed in the upstream are Linux, Python 3.10–3.13, and `uv`; mjwarp training requires a CUDA GPU. The following command comes from the upstream instructions in [ and ](https://github.com/Motphys/Uni-SuperMimic#installation), and it is run in the root directory of the repository:

```bash
git clone https://github.com/Motphys/Uni-SuperMimic.git
cd Uni-SuperMimic
uv run unisupermimic-train --help
uv run tools/prepare_supermimic_assets.py
uv run tools/prepare_supermimic_assets.py --validate-only
```

Resource preparation will obtain G1 model and LAFAN1 action data; the upstream description indicates that the complete LAFAN1 set includes 40 action files. The checkpoint indicates that the resource verification command is completed and no missing items are reported. For model names, repository names, command names, parameter names, and abbreviations, keep them as they are.

```bash
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 uv run unisupermimic-train \
  training.log_dir=runs/supermimic_mjwarp_001
```

This command uses the upstream default LAFAN1 configuration, and the training results are written to the specified directory. Adequate GPU resources are required for training. When selecting the Motrix backend, `task=g1_super_mimic/motrix` should be added in the upstream manner, and the corresponding recovery and evaluation should maintain the same backend configuration.

If the matching training run directory and checkpoint exist, you can execute:

```bash
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 uv run unisupermimic-eval \
  --backend mjwarp \
  --ckpt runs/supermimic_mjwarp_001/ckpt_012000.pt
```

The evaluation starts from the first frame of the action. Disable observation and action noise and run the entire clip; the evaluation results are saved in the execution directory. Checkpoints are also released by the upstream, and a matching action library, model, and configuration must be prepared according to the instructions before use. Video export supports specifying `jumps1_subject1` and other clips. For specific parameters, see the upstream video export instructions ](https://github.com/Motphys/Uni-SuperMimic#video-export) and [.

## How to Understand the Results of the Author's Report

The upstream dataset for LAFAN1 reports 40 actions, a normalized return of 0.827227 for `ckpt_012000.pt`, and 0/40 failed actions. Its BONES-SEED results were obtained using a different large-scale action library and configuration, and the metrics from different datasets cannot be directly compared as representing the same conditions. The phrase “approximately 40 minutes” in the video text refers to the author’s description of a specific run; the actual training time should also include hardware, backend, dataset, iteration count, and evaluation method.
